newsitem.title: USA: TCI debt jumps; more trust pfds to hit US corp mart.
newsitem.headline: TCI debt jumps; more trust pfds to hit US corp mart.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond market activity on Friday morning focused on Standard & Poor's decision to affirm TCI Communications Inc debt ratings, as well as the large number of new trust preferred issues expected to hit the market later in the day, market sources said.
TCI's 7-7/8 percent bonds of 2013 tightened by 20 basis points on Friday morning immediately following the S&P's announcement to hold the cable company's rating at BBB-minus.
Later in the morning, several traders said the market had overreacted to the news.
In the new-issue market, several large trust preferred deals by banks were expected to hit the market on Friday.
A unit of Chase Manhattan Bank was expected to sell $300 million of these securities via Chase Securities Inc, market sources said.
Earlier on Friday morning, First Chicago NBD priced $250 million floating-rate trust preferred deal via Lehman Brothers Inc, they added.
Also on Friday morning, a trust set up by Citicorp sold $450 million of capital trust preferred securities through a Citicorp Securities Inc-led syndicate.
No new high-yield offerings were expected to price on Friday, according to market sources.

Late on Thursday, Perez Companc SA, an Argentine oil and gas company, sold $300 million in notes due 2004 in a 144a private placement via Morgan Stanley & Co Inc. The notes, which were rated B1/BB-minus, were priced at par to yield nine percent.
The deal was increased to $300 million from an original size of $200 million due to strong investor demand, sources said

Also on Thursday, Derlan Manufacturing Inc sold $110 million in senior unsecured notes in a 144a private placement via BT Securities Inc. The notes, rated B3/B-plus, were priced at par to yield 10 percent.
